newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab African International Bank offering 5-yr FRNs.
newsitem.headline: Arab African International Bank offering 5-yr FRNs.

text.p: Arab African International Bank said on Monday it was offering five-year floating-rate notes worth 300 million pounds ($88 million) for two months starting March 5.

The notes will pay interest every three months, at 0.25 percentage points above the average yield on 91-day treasury bills over the three-month period, it said. The average yield on 91-day bills is now a fraction below 10 percent.
If the treasury does not issue 91-day bills, the interest will be 2.75 percentage points below the Central Bank discount rate, which now stands at 13 percent.
The bank may close the issue 10 days after March 5 if it is already fully subscribed, the bank said.
The notes will be in units of 1,000 pounds and the bank will issue them in lots of one, five, 10, 25, 50 and 100 notes, it said. The fee for issuing them will be two pounds per note.
The agents for the subscription are National Bank of Egypt.
The bank said it made net profits of $1.88 million in the first nine months of calendar 1996, compared with $12.1 million in all of 1995 and $10.2 million in 1994.
But it forecast that net profits would rise to $15.576 million in 1997 and $18.789 million in 1998. They would keep rising through the next years to reach $33.582 million in 2002.
On September 30, 1996, it had total assets of $812.39 million, against $822.00 million at the end of 1995.
Shareholders' funds were worth $141.48 million at the end of the nine-month period, against $139.6 million at the end of 1995, it said.
The bank has paid-in capital of $100 million. The Central Bank of Egypt and the Kuwaiti Finance Ministry own 49.37 percent each and other shareholders the balance of 1.26 percent.
